To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypoxia-mediated impairment of the mitochondrial respiratory activity of infected Mφ inhibits the bactericidal capacity of Mφ against E. coli and S. aureus, independently of ROI or NOS2.
hypoxia impairs the bactericidal capacity of Mϕ, and this is not due to a lack in PHOX and NOD2 activity but is caused by an impaired activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chains.
the bactericidal function of macrophages against E. coli and S. aureus is impaired under hypoxic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how macrophages (the most important phagocyte in the innate immune system) kill invading bacteria.
a previously unknown antimicrobial activity of the respiratory chain and provides evidence that the respiratory chain is a novel target of hypoxia.
the question how hypoxia influences the antibacterial effector functions of macrophages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bactericidal capacity of macrophages is impaired during hypoxia due to an inhibition of the mitochondrial respiratory activity, which in turn leads to an insufficient production of antimicrobial effector molecules.
the bactericidal capacity of the mitochondria is impaired in hypoxic macrophages, which is at least partly independent of the PHOX- and NOS2-mediated generation of ROI and NO, respectively.
the hypoxia-mediated impairment of mitochondrial activity in Mϕ inhibits the antibacterial activity of these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia-mediated impairment of the mitochondrial activity is a novel mechanism of bacterial survival within phagocytes.
hypoxia-mediated impairment of the mitochondrial respiratory activity of Mϕ inhibits the antibacterial activity of the host against E. coli and S. aureus.
the bactericidal capacity of Mϕ is reduced during hypoxia, and this is due to a hypoxia-induced inhibition of mitochondrial respiratory chain activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial respiratory chain is an essential component of the Mϕ antibacterial effector system.
mitochondria are important antimicrobial effectors and that their activity is compromised during hypoxia.
